_readme: PHYSICALLY BROKEN HARDWARE — an inventory of rigs that are damaged right now.
THIS IS NOT THE RETIRED SAFETY-LIMIT SYSTEM. Do not confuse the two.
config/hardware-safety.json was emptied on 2026-08-20 by operator ruling ('You can remove these
for all characters, we don't need them ever again') and that ruling stands: software refuses no
operator command, clamps no angle, caps no duration and serializes no rail.
This file does something narrower and different. It records which parts are PHYSICALLY DAMAGED,
so that code choosing a part ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE — an automated test suite, a diagnostic
script, a fleet sweep — does not pick a broken one. The operator may still drive anything listed
here, deliberately, from the UI or the API. Nothing in the runtime request path reads this file.
Why it exists: tests/system/parts-api.test.js was written to skip these parts and selected them
through safetyLimits.isTestSafePart(). When hardware-safety.json was emptied, that helper began
returning true for every part, so the loop picked servos[0] — Orlok's dead Elbow on the fused
rail that has repeatedly blown. The guard inverted into selecting the worst possible part, and
npm run test:system physically drove the Elbow and the Bow actuator on 2026-08-21.
Remove an entry when the operator repairs the hardware, not to make a test pass.

4._note: Sir Dragomir — head servo only. See docs/hardware/OPERATOR-TODO.md §C and docs/hardware/BENCH-CHECKLIST.md K1/K2.

1.reason: Head Servo (goBILDA Stingray-2, 900° multi-turn, PCA9685 ch4) — dead-channel suspect (K1 verdict pending), and its calibration profile still maps it as 0-180 over the same pulse span, so one commanded degree is five real degrees of rotation: an automated sweep can wrap the head cabling. Advisory like every entry here — the operator may still drive it deliberately; automated pickers must not.

3._note: Orlok is the only physically damaged rig as of 2026-08-21 (operator, verbatim: 'only orlock is physically hacked with bad back left arm forearm and elbow').

2.reason: Left Arm of Manipulation — operator reports the left arm is physically damaged.

3.reason: Bow At The Waist — operator reports the back is physically damaged. Also has a self-contradicting BTS7960 wiring record: the part description says RPWM=21/LPWM=19 while the data fields say rpwmPin:19/lpwmPin:21, and that swap inverts direction, so 'extend' may physically retract.

4.reason: Elbow — electrically dead, and shares a fused rail with part 5 that has repeatedly blown. Was found on 2026-08-21 still energized at 1308.6us after a test run, which is a stall-current path.

5.reason: Forearm Rotation — operator reports the forearm is physically damaged. Travel was never measured. Shares the fused rail with part 4.
